overview: Student Attendance Early Support addresses staff search multiple approved sources manually and struggle to preserve permissions and version context in education and research operations. The first proof of value uses attendance records, coursework completion and consented welfare notes. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is days to first reviewed support contact, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.
kpi: days to first reviewed support contact

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: attendance records, coursework completion and consented welfare notes; define days to first reviewed support contact and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from University CIO / Academic Program Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including golden question set with prompt-injection and authorization tests.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for days to first reviewed support contact
